text:
maria: Heads up — did a profiling pass on prod traffic this morning. saw a latency tail bump after we increased the batching hold window to 12ms. copying notes here for quick sync.
aj: hmm, is that across all models or specific families?
maria: mostly for the decoder-heavy models (long context) — KV cache hit rates dropped a bit and kernel selection started choosing the fallback path more often.
ryan: fallback path as in the non-quantized kernel? or the slower attention kernel?
maria: the attention kernel. profiling shows a ~15% longer kernel time when batch shapes became more heterogeneous.
sanjay: that tracks — with a longer hold window we accumulate more variable-length requests, which breaks the perf assumptions for the fused attention path.
elaine: any changes to queue admission rules recently? we adjusted token_budget targets last week.
maria: yes, token_budget per-admit was nudged up to 1.6x. idea was to reduce starved batches but seems to increase shape variance.
aj: can we bias batching towards length-homogeneous grouping? e.g., hold slightly longer if we expect more short requests, or split long ones into aggressive small batches?
ryan: we experimented with dynamic batch formation based on histogram bucketing. it helps but increases scheduler complexity and can delay pkts.
elaine: proposal: add a soft bucket affinity signal in the queue admission metadata. if a request indicates expected length (client-provided or estimated), prefer admitting into matching batch window. keep default as current for backward compat.
sanjay: sounds reasonable. need fallback: if affinity causes starvation for low-volume buckets, we should relax after X ms.
maria: also noticed KV cache hit ratio dips from 78% -> 65% in the interval where the hold window increased. I think larger windows mixed long/short contexts cause more cache misses due to differing prefix alignments.
aj: could be prefetch or eviction thrashing. do we have the eviction trace?
aria: (typo, maria) I attached a small snippet to the thread in profiler — paste below: 
```
# sample trace excerpt
batch_id=4921 shapes=[64x128, 32x512, 16x1024] kernel=attention_fallback time_ms=12.4 kv_hit=false
batch_id=4922 shapes=[64x128,64x128] kernel=attention_fast time_ms=3.1 kv_hit=true
```
aj: ugh. that pattern will absolutely punish the fast kernel.
ryan: short-term mitigation: revert hold window from 12ms -> 8ms for the affected shards and run the affinity experiment on a canary.
elaine: add a circuit on the admit path: if observed kernel_choice_mismatch_rate > 10% over 1 minute, reduce hold window and decrement token_budget. That would be a soft-shed behavior rather than hard 429.
sanjay: agreed. let's not throw 429s immediately. soft-reject path could return a light-weight hint to clients: `retry-later:window=8ms` and increment a counter for telemetry.
maria: can we prototype the metric kernel_choice_mismatch_rate quickly? I can add a counter in the runtime and surface it to the console.
aj: i'll add the admit-policy toggle flag: `admit.affinity=true/false`, `admit.soft_threshold=0.10`, `admit.hold_ms_override` for quick toggles.
ryan: also add a small A/B: group A uses affinity+soft-shed, group B keeps current. monitor p50/p95/p99 + kv_hit + kernel_mismatch.
maria: launch canary this afternoon after a short rollout plan. i'll capture samples and share a condensed perf summary. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/exp/admit-affinity canary -> shard-3 at 2026-03-17T22:30:00Z
elaine: reminder: if we do any client-facing retry hints we must update docs + SDKs to avoid noisy client retries. add a rate cap on retries server-side.
aj: will add `Retry-After` semantics to the hint header.
sanjay: one more note — kernel selection model needs a tie-breaker when shapes are mixed: prefer fast kernel if >65% of tokens match the fast shape, otherwise prefer fallback. might reduce oscillation.
maria: (typo correction) maria: good call. i'll include that tie-breaker in the experiment.
ryan: ok team, action items: maria add metric + summary; aj add flags + retry header; sanjay implement tie-breaker; elaine prepare doc blurb; i'll coordinate canary rollout. check-in in 3 hours.
maria: thanks. I'll post profiler dumps in #eng-runtime/postmortems if things look bad.
aj: ack.
elaine: ack.
perf-bot: telemetry alarms: kernel_choice_mismatch_rate > 10% (will alert #eng-runtime if triggered)
